title: Wringer untracked-file identities
description: `untracked.json` — git's IDENTITY for every UNTRACKED file in the working tree when the gates ran. A SIBLING of manifest.json, like digests.json and for the same reason: `wringer.evidence.v1` is frozen, so the tree's untracked state arrives as its own file rather than as a manifest key, and a reader that does not know this file ignores it. It exists because git cannot diff a file it has never seen: `diff.patch` is silent about untracked content, so without this a content-only edit to a new file between `wring verify` and `wring deliver` was undetectable. Untracked is not ignored: anything in .gitignore never appears here, so the cost is bounded by what `git status` already reports. Absent from a bundle whose tree had nothing untracked — an empty file would be a claim about a state that never existed. Supersedes `wringer.untracked.v1`, which recorded a bare sha256 of the bytes a gate could READ: that follows symlinks, and git commits mode 120000 plus a blob holding the link TEXT, so v1 pinned a different object from the one being delivered. v1 remains published and frozen and every v1 bundle stays valid; `wring deliver` reads a v1 bundle exactly as it reads a bundle written before this file existed.

algorithm.description: The digest algorithm. Named rather than assumed, so a future change is a value rather than a silent reinterpretation of every existing file.

files.description: Repo-relative POSIX path -> `"<mode>:<digest>"`, where mode is the one git would put in the tree and digest is the sha256 of the payload git would store: a regular file's content for 100644 and 100755, and the LINK TEXT for 120000. Mode and digest are one string so that a type flip — a file replaced by a symlink to a file with the same bytes — is a digest change by construction rather than by a reader remembering to compare two keys. Two literal values stand in for a path that has no such identity: "unreadable" for a real file whose bytes could not be read (a permissions problem, after v2 made dangling and directory-targeted symlinks recordable), and "unsupported" for a path that is neither a regular file nor a symlink, which git would not commit either. `wring deliver` refuses on both: a path nobody could check is a path nobody verified, and silence would be the friendlier lie.
